title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 140 (Rights of surety on payment or performance)

content.overview: Section 140 provides that where a guaranteed debt has become due, or default of the principal debtor to perform a guaranteed duty has taken place, the surety, upon payment or performance of all that he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor.
content.glance: On payment or performance of all the surety is liable for, the surety is subrogated to the creditor's rights against the principal debtor.
content.study: Where a guaranteed debt has become due, or default of the principal debtor to perform a guaranteed duty has taken place, the surety, upon payment or performance of all that he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor. Current-law framing: full payment/performance of the surety's liability triggers subrogation.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where a guaranteed debt has become due, or default of the principal debtor to perform a guaranteed duty has taken place, the surety, upon payment or performance of all that he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor.

examples.title: Subrogation after full payment
examples.body: Surety pays the full amount for which he is liable after default. Surety is invested with the creditor's rights against the principal debtor.

hypotheticals.question: Surety pays only part of what he is liable for. Does Section 140 fully apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 140 requires payment or performance of all that the surety is liable for before the surety is invested with all the creditor's rights.

enhancement.definition: Where a guaranteed debt has become due, or default of the principal debtor to perform a guaranteed duty has taken place, the surety, upon payment or performance of all that he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Full satisfaction by the surety invests the surety with the creditor's rights against the principal debtor (subrogation).
essentialIngredients: Debt due or default in guaranteed duty
Payment or performance of all the surety is liable for
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 140 provides for subrogation: once the surety has paid or performed all that he is liable for after the debt is due or default has occurred, the surety steps into the creditor's rights against the principal debtor.
examples: Full payment by surety invests surety with creditor's rights.
distinctions: Section 140 is subrogation against the principal debtor; Section 141 is benefit of securities; Section 145 is implied indemnity.
keyTakeaways: Surety is subrogated to creditor's rights on full payment or performance.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-140
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: s-140 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
